paper: step 8. Provisional Section 3.3. The commons reference evaluation model is a trained artifact.
adr: Diagnostic checkpoint sweep. Same corpus, taxonomy, and gate as the training recipe. This run does not decide the published pin; it samples the loss curve so a sweet spot or a capacity ceiling is a measured fact.

base.note: Read at run time from the manifest. repoId here is a pin that must match. Do not train Qwen3-0.6B-Base. Do not swap the base in this diagnostic.

framework.whyNotUnsloth: 0.6B plus 3936 short examples does not need Unsloth's memory path. The standard stack is the one a reader can follow without a third training runtime.
framework.torch: supplied by the GPU image; not pinned here so a CUDA wheel is not overwritten

train.evalDatasetNote: The held-out suite is the final gate, never a training or hyperparameter split. The sweep gates after the fact. It does not train against the suite.

sweep.purpose: Sample the training curve between the underfit (loss ~0.05, recall collapse) and overfit (loss ~0.003, extra-class fires) endpoints. One GPU run, many gated checkpoints. Not a second gate, not a label change, not a model swap.

llamaCpp.note: convert_hf_to_gguf.py then llama-quantize Q8_0. The run records the resolved commit in checkpoints.json.

time.estimate: Training three epochs of 0.6B LoRA is minutes on an 80GB card. Six merge-plus-Q8_0 exports and six 187-item CPU gates dominate the wall time and should still finish well under three hours. If the train loop itself is still running after 90 minutes, stop and report.
